title: Principality of Svaneti
capsule: The Principality of Svaneti was a semi-autonomous highland polity controlling the upper Inguri and Nenskra valleys in the Greater Caucasus, in what is now northwestern Georgia. It emerged as a distinct entity after the fragmentation of the unified Georgian kingdom in the late fifteenth century, governed successively by the Gelovani and Dadeshkeliani noble houses under the nominal suzerainty of the Kingdom of Imereti. Russian suzerainty was accepted in 1833 as the Romanov empire consolidated the Caucasus; the principality ended violently in 1857 when Prince Konstantin Dadeshkeliani murdered a Russian military administrator, was court-martialled, and executed, after which Russia formally annexed the territory in 1858.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's territory is geographically well defined by Caucasian valley topography; exact boundaries with neighbouring Georgian principalities are not precisely mapped in historical sources.
